title: November 12: TärinäSR — shaking-camera phase diversity becomes measurable image resolution
summary: TarinaSR directly inherits SihtiSR's one-frame learned filters and implements classical motion-aligned multi-frame super-resolution by iterative back-projection from a 16-frame ring. The ring and phase metaphors converge with GoldOpus and PhaseLockedPredictiveCoding, but the 2026 code solves spatial subpixel registration, not temporal-phase XOR. The eight-scene synthetic benchmark reports large PSNR gains and meaningful whole-pixel/averaging controls; realistic synthetic lens/JPEG stress reduces the gain. Multi-frame super-resolution and natural camera-tremor sampling are established prior art, and gains on real handheld-camera footage are unmeasured.

nodes.claim: TärinäSR (TarinaSR): a small readable browser implementation of multi-frame ×2 grayscale super-resolution. Phase-correlation plus blurred-image Lucas–Kanade registers small spatial shifts/rotations; a ring stores 16 frames and repeatedly back-projects observation residuals into a high-resolution state initialized by SihtiSR.
nodes.survived: Source-reported 8 standard scikit-image photos, simulated subpixel motion/noise: mean 37.42 dB PSNR (16-frame ring), compared with 31.86 dB SihtiSR single frame and 30.90 dB bicubic. Two-frame 32.57, four-frame 34.14, eight-frame 36.01. Registered averaging plus SihtiSR scored 31.64; whole-low-res-pixel shifts 32.05, supporting subpixel phase diversity rather than mere averaging. With synthetic lens blur σ=0.7, JPEG quality 85 and small rotation, mean 32.06 dB with correct lens parameter vs 29.99 SihtiSR, 30.83 without lens calibration.
nodes.killed: Not a new super-resolution method: iterative back-projection dates to Irani & Peleg (1991), and Pixel-phone burst SR exploits hand tremor (Wronski et al., 2019). Eight synthesized rigid-motion scenes, not a held-out real-video camera benchmark; no proof of gain on actual phone footage, moving scenes, perspective changes or unknown strong optics. Synthetic demo generates input with its own forward warp; the separate Python benchmark uses scipy transforms. This is not native GN27, XOR memory, a learned temporal phase hub or transformer acceleration.
nodes.era: November 12: from periodic-memory rings to subpixel image reconstruction

edges.why: TarinaSR directly copies sihtisr.py, sihti.js and model.* unchanged, uses the SihtiSR single-frame output as its initial high-resolution image, then adds registration and iterative multi-frame back-projection.
The new work explicitly credits GoldOpus's circulating ring and turns the prior negative timing-jitter motif into subpixel sample diversity; no GoldOpus neuron or code reuse is claimed.

Both use a shared alignment idea and memory/residual comparison, but TarinaSR estimates *spatial* subpixel camera motion while PhaseLockedPredictiveCoding chose *temporal* offsets in a periodic template. No common implementation of a phase hub is asserted.

motifs.title: In temporal memory jitter is error; in multi-frame imaging spatial jitter can supply missing samples
motifs.description: GoldOpus's event jitter broke a precisely timed predictive ring; TarinaSR instead models frame-to-frame rigid subpixel motion and reuses differently phased spatial observations to recover high-resolution detail. The subpixel-versus-whole-pixel ablation identifies the information source. This is established multi-frame super-resolution, not a newly discovered law or an original GN result.
